name: Filip Waeytens
why_notable: Co-wrote dnsenum with tixxDZ in the mid-2000s: a multithreaded Perl script built to gather as much DNS information about a domain as possible and to discover its non-contiguous IP blocks through zone transfers, brute force, class C netrange whois and reverse sweeps. He hosted it on Google Code and then GitHub (fwaeytens/dnsenum); after maintenance passed to Network Silence and the dnsenum2 fork, the tool kept his design and credits and still ships in Kali, Debian and Ubuntu as a staple of DNS footprinting.
